comments.body:
Thanks for catching the retired model, @pcbeingused333. I pushed a follow-up in 815160d784c5495cd214860aeabcdb9b3d7bfe55 to make sure the examples produce real responses with the replacement settings.

Terra was a reasonable choice given the deprecation guidance. We went with `gpt-5.6-luna` because these examples ask for short customer-service replies, so the smaller, lower-cost model is a sensible default. We haven't run a Luna-versus-Terra quality comparison.

The main correctness issue was the token budget: `max_completion_tokens` covers internal reasoning as well as the visible answer. With default reasoning and only 150–200 tokens, a call can exhaust its budget before returning any text, and the existing helpers then return a placeholder or template. Both examples now disable reasoning and allow 512 completion tokens.

I also added the explicit `openai/` prefix for LiteLLM, since its cached model list didn't recognize the bare Luna name, and raised the example requirements to SDK versions we tested: `openai>=2.8.0` and `litellm>=1.80.0`. The three comparison agents now use the helper's default, and alternative providers don't receive Luna's reasoning setting.

Validation: seven offline regression tests pass at those minimum versions, and four live calls through the helpers returned non-empty Luna answers, all finishing normally with zero reasoning tokens. Ruff, formatting, and compilation pass. The existing example docstring/type-check issues are recorded in the PR description; we haven't exercised the full ZenML pipelines.
Hi @strickvl, friendly ping: this one is approved and green on our side. Happy to rebase or adjust anything if that helps it land. Thanks!
